posts.title: Actually, Simulation Bias Is Real — Models Live in Training, Runtime Is Where They Break
posts.description: Models are trained in simulation. That sounds obvious until you watch a model fail in runtime. Note on framing : “simulation bias” as used here is a proposed unifying label for three related but distinct failure modes. It is not a settled term of art — the cited papers treat these issues separately, and the label is an editorial lens, not a claim of consensus. The three: Offline training signals.
